append.text: **Ps 21:2 *réspice in me* → *olhai para mim*** (the row's verb with the Latin's *in me*; the Greek here is πρόσχες μοι, the Latin's verb followed); **21:20 *cónspice* (only here, also πρόσχες) → *olhai para a minha defesa*** — one Portuguese verb, as the Greek has one. Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked.

Ps 21:2 *quare me dereliquísti?* → *por que me abandonastes?* — the Passion's cry (Mt 27:46, Mk 15:34 Vulgate have *Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?*, fetched: not the psalm's wording). *desamparastes* (MS1932) is the option.
Ps 21:2 *verba delictórum meórum* → *as palavras das minhas faltas*; the blind reader heard sins first, 'what I lack' second.
Ps 21:3 *clamábo per diem … et nocte* → *clamarei durante o dia … e de noite* (MS1932's pair): the row held beside *nocte*; *de dia* is the option.

**Ps 21:3, the noun (named here): *et non ad insipiéntiam mihi* → *e não será para a minha insensatez*** — draft 1's verbless *e não para a minha insensatez* was heard by the blind reader as '*não para*' = does not STOP (*parar*); the copula *será* (the stylist's) mends it. Open as the Latin (not folly in me / not to my folly).

**Ps 21:4 *Tu autem in sancto hábitas* → *Mas vós habitais no lugar santo*** (the row, DRB, MS1932; the Greek's plural ἐν ἁγίοις not followed). The apposition *laus Israël* → *vós, louvor de Israel*: bare, it was heard as the holy place's name.
Ps 21:6 *non sunt confúsi* → *não foram envergonhados* (D15); heard as 'not humiliated'.
Ps 21:7 *oppróbrium hóminum* → *a afronta dos homens*; heard as insult suffered.

**Ps 21:7 *abjéctio plebis* (only here) → *o desprezo do povo***: its Greek ἐξουδένημα is of the root of 118:22 ἐξουδένωσιν (*contémptum*) and of 21:25 ἐξουδένωσεν (*non sprevit* → *não desprezou*), so the psalm's own echo is kept. Options *o refugo*, MS1932 *a abjeção*.
Ps 21:25 *non sprevit* → *não desprezou* (answers 21:7 *o desprezo*, one Greek root).
**derídere, Ps 21:8 *derisérunt me* → *escarneceram de mim*** — the verb this row keeps for derídere (MS1932). The blind reader listed *escarneceram* as unknown; kept. *zombaram* is the option.

**Ps 21:9 *erípiat eum* (no source named; the mockers' words) → *que ele o liberte*** — the row's own conclusion (*libertar* never fails), with *livrar* left to 21:5 *liberásti*. Mt 27:43 (Vulgate, fetched) has *liberet nunc, si vult eum* — another wording. See the new row *éruere*.
Ps 21:9 *quóniam vult eum* → *porque o quer* (17:20's build); the blind reader heard 'because the Lord wants to save him' — near; *porque lhe quer bem* is the option.

Ps 21:10 *In te projéctus sum ex útero* (ἐπὶ σὲ ἐπερρίφην) → *Sobre vós fui lançado desde o seio materno* (DRB *cast upon thee*); *Em vós* would be heard as 'into you'. Heard as 'entrusted to God from birth'.
**Ps 21:11 *De ventre matris meæ Deus meus es tu* → *Desde o ventre da minha mãe vós sois o meu Deus*** — the formula held; no reader remarked.
Ps 21:11 *ne discésseris a me* → *não vos afasteis de mim* — which is why 21:20 *ne elongáveris … a me* (another verb, μακρύνω) is *não ponhais longe de mim* (see the new row *elongáre*).
Ps 21:12 *non est qui ádjuvet* → *não há quem auxilie* (no object, as the Latin); no reader remarked.
Ps 21:13, 21:17 *Circumdedérunt me* ×2 → *Cercaram-me … me cercaram*, each followed by *obsidére* → *sitiar* (new row).

**Ps 21:13 *tauri pingues* → *touros gordos*; 21:30 *omnes pingues terræ* → *todos os gordos da terra*** (the psalm's echo kept). The blind reader heard 21:30 FIRST as people with fat bodies, the prosperous second — the Latin's image; *os ricos* (MS1932) is the option there.
Ps 21:14 *sicut leo rápiens et rúgiens* → *como um leão que arrebata e ruge*; *arrebata* listed as unknown by the blind reader, kept.
Ps 21:16 *in púlverem mortis deduxísti me* → *e me fizestes descer ao pó da morte* (D25, as named); heard as 'God brought me to death or near it'.

**Ps 21:16 *lingua mea adhǽsit fáucibus meis* → *a minha língua se colou à minha garganta*** — a physical sticking: *se apegou* (draft 1, this row) was heard by the stylist as affection before touch, so the row's own option (DM1962 *colar-se*) is taken there. Proposal: *apegar-se* where the soul clings (118:25, 31; 62:9), *colar-se* where a body part sticks (21:16; 101:6 *adhǽsit os meum carni meæ*, 136:6a *Adhǽreat lingua mea fáucibus meis* — grep before use).
Ps 21:16 *fáucibus meis* → *à minha garganta* (the row; λάρυγγι); *paladar* the option. No reader remarked.

**Ps 21:16 *Áruit tamquam testa virtus mea* (ἰσχύς) → *O meu vigor secou-se como um caco*:** a man's bodily strength drying up — *poder* would be authority, *força* is fortitúdo's. MS1932's *vigor*. **Proposal: virtus of a man's own strength → *vigor*** (30:11 *infirmáta est … virtus mea*, 37:11 *dereliquit me virtus mea*, 70:9 *dum defécerit virtus mea* — grep before use); *poder* stays for God's (*in virtúte tua*) and for 17:33, 40. Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked.

**Ps 21 met the collision this row foretold, and rules it for review: two Latin words six verses apart, two Greek words (21:17 *concílium malignántium* = συναγωγὴ πονηρευομένων; 21:23, 21:26 *ecclésia* = ἐκκλησία), so two Portuguese words.** *ecclésia → assembleia* everywhere (see the new row *ecclésia*); *concílium* here → ***a congregação dos malvados***, on D15's test with synagóga → congregação (συναγωγή). The Greek behind concílium varies (read in the parallels files): 1:5 βουλή, 21:17 συναγωγή, 25:4 συνεδρίου, 39:11 συναγωγῆς. **Proposal: concílium → *congregação* where it is συναγωγή (21:17, 39:11); 1:5 (βουλή) and 25:4 (συνέδριον) decide locally — 1:5's *assembleia* would then share the word with ecclésia in another psalm.** Passed the Latinist twice; the blind reader heard 'a group of wicked people' (the cães as its image), never a religious order.
Ps 21:17 *concílium* (συναγωγή) takes this row's word: *a congregação dos malvados me sitiou* — see *concílium*.
Ps 21:17 *concílium malignántium* → *a congregação dos malvados* (D24); no reader remarked.

**fódere is split by its object (Ps 21:17b):** with a pit (56:7, 93:13) *cavar*, as this row says; with hands and feet *Fodérunt manus meas et pedes meos* → ***Perfuraram as minhas mãos e os meus pés*** — L&S *fodio* transf. 'to prick, pierce, wound, stab' (*latus fodere*, *guttura cultro*). See the new row *fódere*.
Not used for 21:17b *fodérunt* (another Latin and Greek verb, ὀρύσσω): that is *perfurar*, so *traspassar* stays this row's.
**Ps 21:18 *consideravérunt … me* (a person as object) → *me observaram***: *me consideraram* is heard as 'esteemed me'. *considerar* stays for things (118:15, 18).
Ps 21:21 *Érue a frámea* → *Arrancai da espada* — the row applied at a place it named.

**Ps 21:22 *et a córnibus unicórnium humilitátem meam* → *e dos chifres dos unicórnios a minha pequenez*** — a local departure: the object to be SAVED (a metonymy for the lowly self, like *únicam meam*); *salvai … a minha humilhação* would be heard as keeping the humiliation, and *leão … humilhação* rhymed at mediant and final. DRB *my lowness*; heard as 'my fragility'. *humilhação* is the option there.
Ps 21:22 *a córnibus unicórnium* → *dos chifres dos unicórnios*; no reader remarked.

**Ps 21:24 *univérsum semen Jacob* (the test D32 named), 21:25 *omne semen Israël*, 21:31 *semen meum* → *descendência* ×3** (one decision `semen`, three slots); no plant image in these verses; *semente* the option. No reader remarked.
Ps 21:25 *non sprevit, neque despéxit deprecatiónem páuperis* → *não desprezou, nem desdenhou a prece do pobre*; no reader stumbled on *desdenhou* this time.
Ps 21:25 *deprecatiónem páuperis* → *a prece do pobre* (a fourth place agrees; not at a cadence).
Ps 21:25b *Nec avértit fáciem suam a me* → *Nem desviou de mim a sua face* (the face formula, 12:1).
Ps 21:3 *et non exáudies* → *e não escutareis*; 21:25b *exaudívit me* → *escutou-me*.
**Ps 21:26 *vota mea reddam* → *pagarei os meus votos*** (a place this row named); the blind reader heard religious promises first ('electoral votes' third).

**Ps 21 (one decision `conspectu`, three slots): 21:26 *vota mea reddam in conspéctu timéntium eum* → *à vista dos que o temem*** (the place of witnesses); **21:28b *adorábunt in conspéctu ejus* and 21:30 *in conspéctu ejus cadent* → *na sua presença*** (with an act of worship; *adorarão à vista dele* is stiff) — the Ps 17 split again. No reader remarked.
Ps 21:27 *Edent páuperes, et saturabúntur* → *Os pobres comerão, e serão saciados* (the row, as named).
Ps 21:27 *qui requírunt eum* (ἐκζητοῦντες) → *os que o procuram* — requírere merged into this row's verb again, on the Greek, as at 118:145 and 13:2.

Ps 21:27 *vivent corda eórum in sǽculum sǽculi* → *viverão os seus corações pelos séculos dos séculos*: the Latinist's minor twice (singular), refused (D27); the stylist asked for the formula first (proparoxytone final) — refused, the Latin's own cadence; option in decision `saeculi`.

**Ps 21:28 *converténtur ad Dóminum univérsi fines terræ* → *Hão de lembrar-se e converter-se ao Senhor*** — D25's exception (men turning to God); heard as 'come to believe in the Lord' first. *voltar-se* the option.
Ps 21:29 *ipse dominábitur géntium* → *e ele dominará as nações*.
Ps 21:32 *justítiam ejus* → *a sua justiça*.

terms: | ecclésia | assembleia (*no meio da assembleia vos louvarei*; *na grande assembleia*) | open — **for a ruling** (with *concílium*) | Ps 21:23, 21:26. Ten lines, ἐκκλησία in all that were read (grep; Greek read at 25:5, 25:12, 39:10): 21:23 (= Heb 2:12, whose Clementine has *in medio ecclesiæ*, fetched), 21:26, 25:5 *Odívi ecclésiam malignántium*, 25:12 *in ecclésiis benedícam te*, 34:18 and 39:10 *in ecclésia magna* (21:26's words), 67:27 *In ecclésiis benedícite Deo*, 88:6 and 149:1 *in ecclésia sanctórum*, 106:32 *in ecclésia plebis*. ***igreja*** (MS1932 *no meio da Igreja*, DRB *church*; the Church's reading of 21:23 through Heb 2:12) was weighed on D19's reasoning for *Christus* and refused: it cannot serve 25:5 (*a igreja dos malvados*), and at 67:27 and 21:26 (*na grande igreja*) it is heard as a building. So one word for all ten, which forces *concílium* elsewhere (row *concílium*). Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked; the blind reader heard *irmãos* (21:23) as the religious community. Option in Ps 21's decision `concilium`: *da igreja / na grande igreja*. |

| éruere | arrancar (*Arrancai da espada, Deus, a minha alma*) | open | Ps 21:21. 13 lines (grep: 21:21, 24:17, 24:20, 31:7, 36:40, 38:9, 42:1, 49:15, 85:13, 88:49 ×2, 143:11 …), nearly always *érue me* with a source (*de, a, ab*); L&S 'pluck out, dig out; rescue'. The Greek is ῥύομαι, as behind liberáre and erípere, but the Latin keeps three verbs and **36:40 sets *liberábit … éruet* side by side**, so not *livrar*. Shares *arrancar* with erípere-with-a-source (the two never stand in one verse — grep before a psalm that has both); 24:20 *et érue me* (no source) and 49:15 *éruam te* will want the erípere row's *libertar*. MS1932 *Livra*. Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked. |

| fódere | perfurar with a body as object (*Perfuraram as minhas mãos e os meus pés*); cavar with a pit (56:7, 93:13) | open | Ps 21:17b — the Latin's (and the Greek's ὤρυξαν) reading, not the Hebrew's. L&S *fodio* 'to dig' and, transferred, 'to prick, pierce, wound, stab'; with hands and feet the Latin verb says piercing. *traspassar* (MS1932) is confígere's (118:120; another Greek verb); *cavaram* (DRB *dug*) is the option. The Gospels do not quote this colon (Mt 27, Mk 15, Jn 19 read in the Vulgate, fetched). Passed the Latinist twice; heard as done by the wicked. |

| elongáre | pôr / ficar longe (*não ponhais longe de mim o vosso auxílio*) | open | Ps 21:20 (μακρύνῃς). 6 lines (grep: 21:20, 54:8 *elongávi fúgiens*, 70:12 *Deus, ne elongéris a me*, 72:27 *qui elóngant se a te*, 87:19 *Elongásti a me amícum*, 108:18). Kept apart from discédere → afastar-se (21:11 in the same psalm) and keeps the Latin's *longe*. **The stylist refused it** ('montado palavra por palavra') and asked for *afasteis*; held — option in Ps 21. 70:12 can read *não fiqueis longe de mim*; 87:19 may need *afastar* after all (a person as object) |
| abjéctio | desprezo (*e o desprezo do povo*) | open | Ps 21:7 only (grep); see *contémptus*. |

| vítulus | bezerro (*Cercaram-me muitos bezerros*) | open | Ps 21:13; 7 lines (grep: 28:6, 49:9, 50:21, 68:32 *vítulum novéllum*, 105:19–20 the golden calf). Draft 1 *novilhos* (MS1932) was unknown to the blind reader; *bezerros* (DRB *calves*) serves 105:19–20 too. 50:21 (the sacrificial *vítulos*) may want *novilhos* locally |

| obsidére | sitiar (*touros gordos me sitiaram … a congregação dos malvados me sitiou*) | open | Ps 21:13, 21:17 — the only two lines (grep), each after *circumdedérunt* → *cercaram*: one verb twice, as the Latin. The blind reader listed *sitiaram* / *sitiou* as unknown; kept (the plain word for a siege; *assediar* is heard as harassment) |
| testa | caco (*secou-se como um caco*) | open | Ps 21:16 only (grep); a potsherd. MS1932 *barro cozido*; *caco de barro* the option. No reader remarked |

| venter / úbera / úterus | ventre / os peitos / o seio materno | open | Ps 21:10–11, 21:15b. **Three body-words in two verses**: venter (γαστήρ, κοιλία) → *ventre* in all three places (21:10, 21:11, 21:15b); *ab ubéribus matris meæ* → *desde os peitos da minha mãe* (the Latinist asked for the plural — MS1932's word; *os seios* would be heard as the same thing as the womb after it); *ex útero* → *desde o seio materno*: bare *seio* is today the breast, *útero* is clinical, and *ventre* is venter's — *materno* stands for no Latin word, it is what makes *seio* mean womb. úterus elsewhere (grep): 57:4, **70:6 *In te confirmátus sum ex útero: de ventre matris meæ tu es protéctor meus*** (a near twin of 21:10–11 — should follow), 109:3 *ex útero ante lucíferum génui te* (decides for itself), 138:13 *de útero matris meæ* (there *do ventre da minha mãe* may collide with nothing — decide locally). Heard: *no meio do meu ventre* as 'inside the belly'; *seio materno* as birth. |

| únicus (*únicam meam*) | a minha única | open | Ps 21:21 (*e a minha única, da mão do cão*, the stylist's order so that the proparoxytone does not close the verse); 34:17 *a leónibus únicam meam* is the twin (grep) — copy it. 24:16 *únicus et pauper sum ego* is another sense (alone). The blind reader heard 'my only soul' first, 'my only life' second |
| unicórnis | unicórnio | working | Ps 21:22 *dos chifres dos unicórnios* — the Latin's (and the Greek's μονόκερως) animal, not the Hebrew's wild ox; 28:6, 77:69, 91:11 (grep). No reader remarked |
| inspícere | fitar (*me observaram e me fitaram*) | open | Ps 21:18 only (grep); DRB *stared*. Listed as unknown by the blind reader; kept (*examinar* is examináre's, *encarar* is confrontation) |

| vestiménta / vestis / sortem míttere | vestes / veste / lançar sortes | open | Ps 21:18 *repartiram entre si as minhas vestes, e sobre a minha veste lançaram sortes*: one root twice, as the Latin (MS1932's *túnica* is St John's word). **The Latinist asked twice (minor) for the singular *lançaram a sorte*; refused** — heard as casting one's fate. 77:54 *sorte divísit* is another build |
| dinumeráre | contar (*contaram todos os meus ossos*) | working | Ps 21:17b; 89:11, 138:18 (grep) |

| apud te | junto de vós (*Junto de vós está o meu louvor*) | open | Ps 21:26 — the Latin's *apud* (DRB *With thee*), not the Greek's παρὰ σοῦ ('from you'); MS1932 *A ti se dirigirá* adds. 129:4 *apud te propitiátio est*, 129:7 *apud Dóminum misericórdia* will meet it (grep before use) |

| manducáre / édere | comer (both) | working | Ps 21:27 *Edent* and 21:30 *Manducavérunt* — one Greek verb (φάγονται / ἔφαγον), one Portuguese; 9 lines of manducáre (grep: 49:13, 58:16, 77:24–25, 77:29, 101:10, 126:2a, 127:2) |

| dispérgere (things, bones) | dispersar, passive (*e foram dispersos todos os meus ossos*) | open | Ps 21:15; one family with 88:11 *dispersísti* (see *dissipáre*, whose people-places took *dispersar*). MS1932 *se desconjuntaram* explains. No reader remarked |

| perto / longe (21:2, 21:12, 21:20) | *longe … perto … pôr longe* | working | Ps 21 plays *longe a salúte mea* (21:2) / *tribulátio próxima* (21:12) / *ne elongáveris* (21:20). 21:12 takes the stylist's *está perto* (the proparoxytone *próxima* at the mediant), which also answers *longe* |
formulas: | *Deus, Deus meus, réspice in me: quare me dereliquísti?* (21:2) | *Deus, meu Deus, olhai para mim: por que me abandonastes?* | working — Ps 21. **The Gospels quote the cry in another Latin**: Mt 27:46 / Mk 15:34 *Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?* (Clementine, fetched to consult/bolls-VULG-40-27.json, -41-15.json). The psalm keeps its own words; *Meu Deus, meu Deus* is the option |

| *divisérunt sibi vestiménta mea, et super vestem meam misérunt sortem* (21:18's second colon = Mt 27:35 word for word in the Clementine; Jn 19:24 has another wording, *Partiti sunt … in vestem meam*) | *repartiram entre si as minhas vestes, e sobre a minha veste lançaram sortes* | working — Ps 21; keep it identical wherever the Office quotes the verse |

| *Narrábo nomen tuum frátribus meis: * in médio ecclésiæ laudábo te* (21:23; Heb 2:12 Clementine *Nuntiabo …*, fetched) | *Narrarei o vosso nome aos meus irmãos: * no meio da assembleia vos louvarei* | open (hangs on *ecclésia*) — Ps 21 |
| *in ecclésia magna* (21:26, 34:18, 39:10) | *na grande assembleia* | open (hangs on *ecclésia*) — Ps 21 |
| *Quóniam Dómini est regnum* (21:29; cf. 3:9 *Dómini est salus*) | *Porque do Senhor é o reino* | working — Ps 21, built as 3:9 |
